question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Italian government during World War II.
question.text: Name this leader of Italy for most of World War II. He was backed by the Blackshirts.
question.clue: His forces overthrew King Zog and Haile Selassie during their invasions of Albania and Ethiopia, but he himself was ousted in 1943 by Victor Emmanuel III.

swap.leadin: A palace in this city contains portraits of all of its rulers except one, whose portrait was replaced by a black sheet as punishment for treason.
swap.text: Name this Italian city at the end of the Adriatic Sea which was a merchant republic ruled by doges such as Enrico Dandolo and dominated Mediterranean commerce for centuries.
swap.answerHtml: the Most Serene Republic of Venice [or Venezia, or La Serenissimà]
swap.answer: the Most Serene Republic of Venice
swap.clue: This republic's leaders participated in the annual "Marriage of the Sea" ceremony using the ceremonial raft Bucentaur.

question.leadin: In 415 BCE, an expedition of over 100 triremes [tri-reems] sailed to this island to attack the city of Syracuse.
question.text: Name this island off the coast of Italy.
question.clue: Roger de Hautevelle defeated a Saracen garrison here, and Peter III of Aragon instigated a rebellion against Charles of Anjou here, which he supported by sending his army to Trapani.

swap.leadin: This family produced three popes, a large bank, and a giant power vacuum in Tuscany after it declined.
swap.text: Name this powerful Italian family that dominated politics in Florence for multiple centuries.
swap.clue: One member of this group excommunicated Martin Luther.

question.leadin: From his prison cell, Carlos the Jackal claimed that a deal for this politician's life fell through because of a PLO official's loose tongue.
question.text: Name this Italian Christian Democrat statesman, who was kidnapped and killed by terrorists of the Red Brigades during the Years of Lead.
question.clue: Inspector Leonardi was in charge of this man's protection, though his warnings about insufficiency of forces were ignored.

swap.leadin: The League of Cambrai was formed in opposition to this city.
swap.text: Name this city famed for its leaders known as doges [pronounced "doajes"] and its gondoliers, who travel along its many canals.
swap.clue: This city-state's hinterland, the "Domini di Terraferma," was partitioned between Austria and the Cisalpine Republic by the provisions of the 1797 Treaty of Campo Formio.

question.leadin: This city became capital of the Western Roman Empire in 402 A.D.
question.text: Name this city, whose namesake "Exarchate" served as the Byzantine stronghold in Italy from 584-751 A.D, when its last exarch was put to death by the Lombards.
question.clue: It became the seat of the Byzantine governor of Italy in the sixth century, and its namesake Cosmography was written around 700.

swap.text: Moro negotiated the Historic Compromise with this Italian political party. During much of the postwar period, it was the largest party of its political orientation in Western Europe.
swap.answerHtml: Italian Communist Party [or PCI; or Partito Comunista Italiano; do not accept or prompt on answers including the word "socialist"]
swap.clue: This organization joined the CLN on the eve of World War II as part of a strategy known as the Salerno turn.

question.leadin: This expedition ended following the successful siege of Gaeta.
question.text: Name this Sicilian expedition which overthrew the Bourbon king Francis II.
question.clue: The primary opponent was Francis II, who was decisively defeated at Milazzo after failing to stop a landing at Marsala.

swap.text: Rodrigo became Pope Alexander VI, while his son Cesare was praised by Machiavelli and his daughter Lucrezia gained an exaggerated reputation for cruelty.
swap.clue: Another member of this family clashed with Pandolfo Malatesta at Rimini, and fought with the Orsinis in Rome before being killed at Viana.

question.leadin: Rodrigo of this family served as Pope Alexander VI.
question.text: What is this family of Spanish origin which included the Cardinal Cesare who convened the papal orgy known as the Banquet of Chestnuts?
question.clue: One member of this family authored the Treaty of Tordesillas and had his rival Savonarolla executed.

swap.text: This plot, named after a prominent Tuscan family, aimed to assassinate Lorenzo and Giuliano de' Medici while they were taking high mass in the Duomo.
swap.clue: Frederico Montelfeltro likely had a battalion waiting in the hills during this event, which left citizens hanging from the walls of the Palazzo Vecchio and tossed into the Arno river.

question.text: Supported by Charles Emmanuel III, Rosa Govone organized a convitti consisting of a series of shelters and textile shops to provide work to young women throughout this duchy. Monarchs of Italy following the 19th-century reunification came from a family named for this duchy's namesake county, who ruled Piedmont-Sardinia.
question.answerHtml: Duchy of Savoy [or Duché de Savoie or Ducato di Savoia; accept County of Savoy; accept House of Savoy or Savoyards]
question.clue: That duke of this region married his son to the sister of Louis XIII, Christine Marie.

swap.text: Many of Boniface's policies were opposed by this medieval faction, which supported the Holy Roman Emperor over the Papacy.
swap.clue: Before winning the battle of Montaperti, this group agreed to the Peace of Constance after it lost the Battle of Legnano, in which it was opposed by the Lombard League.

question.text: This name, because of the number of bullets fired, was given to the period of unrest from the late 1960s to the early 1980s culminating in the assassination of Prime Minister Aldo Moro.
question.clue: This period was preceded by a series of violent strikes known as the Hot Autumn.

swap.leadin: During this battle, the Arditi Corps earned the nickname "the Caimans of the Piave" for swimming back and forth across the frigid Piave River to carry messages.
swap.text: Name this 1918 victory for Armando Diaz, who had replaced Luigi Cadorna the previous year, which led to the Armistice of Villa Giusti.
swap.clue: This battle fought exactly one year after Caporetto, which led directly to the Armistice of Villa Giusti. This battle marked the end of World War One on the Italian front.

question.leadin: Name these places ruled by the Gonzaga family.
question.text: In 1536, Federico II Gonzaga gained control of this region in Piedmont from a branch of the Palaiologos [pay-lee-AH-loh-gos] family. A nobleman from this region founded the Kingdom of Thessalonica after leading the Fourth Crusade in the conquest of Constantinople.

swap.text: The forces of this Lombard king were smashed by Charlemagne at the capture of Pavia in 774 CE.
swap.clue: This leader's people were profiled by his rival's courtier, Paul the Deacon, who sought the hand of this man's daughter for his Lord.

question.text: This chief of staff of the Italian Army lost his position to Armando Diaz after getting his ass handed to him at Caporetto.
question.clue: This Italian general from World War I who was dismissed after his army was shoved back at the Battle of Caporetto.

swap.leadin: Answer some stuff about a group of barbarians, FTPE.
swap.text: The last stand of these barbarians ended with the death of the king Teias, who had tried to continue the rebellion against the Byzantines led by their prior king, Totila. Queen Amalasuntha was another noteworthy ruler of these people.
swap.clue: After the capture of Widin in the 560s, this people more or less vanished.
